assessments.reasoning: Four contiguous parts cover all 60,636 bytes of SPDX’s commit-pinned json/details/CC-BY-NC-SA-2.0-DE.json, reported SHA-256 8b828e48678c361cb88dc08ec1047b67222389e1d3acda45de9d2a83551743f3. The file gives isDeprecatedLicenseId false, German licenseText with §1(b) and §8(f), name “Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial Share Alike 2.0 Germany”, the exact licenseId and both /legalcode citations. The template and HTML are generated fields within the same record.

GitHub’s API for spdx/license-list-data returns annotated tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b, named v3.29.0. Its object.type is commit and object.sha is 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, exactly the detail-file revision. The API reports an unsigned tag. Repository provenance supports this target mapping without a signature-authentication claim.

The exact URL in both SPDX fields yielded Creative Commons’ German page, with the measured digest d88be489f05079a292baa8faf4bdf81153c2748198da6d4a654428993749cea4. Its heading reads “Namensnennung — Nicht-kommerziell — Weitergabe unter gleichen Bedingungen 2.0” and its separate identifier reads “CC BY-NC-SA 2.0 DE”. The head declares https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/2.0/de/legalcode.de as rel="canonical". The distinct URL is preserved as publisher metadata.

The cited publisher page’s §8(f), read across its second and third parts, says “Auf diesen Lizenzvertrag findet das Recht der Bundesrepublik Deutschland Anwendung.” The SPDX licenseText reproduces that sentence. This supports the German textual context while preserving the 2.0 publisher title exactly. The repeated passage has shared lineage and supplies no separate legal determination.

challenge.method: Traced the annotated tag to its target and compared that commit with the detail-file path. Compared the record’s ID, English name, German text and two citation fields with the publisher heading, separate identifier, HTML canonical link, license landing URL and linked deed. Tested substitution of an unported record or a 3.0 Deutschland record.
challenge.results: The exact DE identifier, 2.0 text and /by-nc-sa/2.0/de/legalcode citation agree. The English SPDX name ends in “2.0 Germany”, and its German licenseText starts with “Creative Commons” before the title. The publisher heading has neither addition. The deed, landing page and /legalcode.de each have a different locator. The exact field values exclude the proposed edition and jurisdiction substitutions without requiring identical wording or bytes.

limitations: SPDX’s isDeprecatedLicenseId value applies to the identifier in release 3.29.0. The Index’s active classification concerns editorial maintenance only. Neither establishes publisher currency, legal effect or a consumer dataset release.

The November publisher digest measures the captured /legalcode response. The September SPDX cross-reference contains a URL and timestamp. Historical byte identity, equivalence with /legalcode.de and semantic or translation equivalence remain unverified.
The evidence covers one generated detail file and one publisher page. Project-wide licensing, downstream grants, interpretation of terms and redistribution rights fall outside the claim.
reasoning: The SPDX v3.29.0 tag targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. At that commit, the generated detail record gives licenseId “CC-BY-NC-SA-2.0-DE”. Both crossRef[0].url and seeAlso[0] equal the inspected publisher URL, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/2.0/de/legalcode. This establishes the claimed documentary correspondence. Under SCES §§3 and 7, the release, data revision and identifier must match, and copied text cannot count as independent corroboration.
